status_reason: Materials (whey and opaque concentrate), target (composition, with laboratory protein and fat as reference) and the process are known, so a provisional first assessment is possible; a dairy NIR application is a reason to test, not proof that it works in this process.
answer: Test NIR on both streams with a separate interface per stream: a transmission/transflection probe with controlled path length for the clear whey and a flush-mounted diffuse-reflection probe for the opaque concentrate, both on the same NIR spectrometer. Compare transmission/transflection and reflection on both streams in a lab trial against independent laboratory protein and fat analyses, and build a separate scatter-corrected PLS calibration per stream. Fluorescence, Raman or MIR ATR can be screened alongside as possible additions for molecular specificity.

inline.headline: Test NIR transmission/transflection on the whey and NIR diffuse reflection on the concentrate, each with its own calibration
inline.probe: Transmission/transflection probe (path usually 1-10 mm) for whey; flush-mounted diffuse-reflection probe for concentrate
inline.install: Separate measuring points in the whey line and in the concentrate pipe or vat, chosen after the interface comparison
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica (350-2400 nm), low-OH silica for long remote cables
inline.test_against: A single transflection probe used on both streams
inline.not_final_because: Variables, ranges, process conditions, installation points and accuracy needs are unknown, and published dairy NIR use only justifies testing; the method must be proven against independent laboratory analyses on the client's own streams.

problems.text: The clear whey and the opaque concentrate behave differently optically: transmission/transflection suits the clear whey and reflection suits the opaque concentrate, so plan a separate interface decision and a separate calibration per stream, and treat one shared interface as a hypothesis to test.
Transmission needs a controlled path length and fails if the product becomes too thick or fat-rich, so check whether the concentrate can be measured this way at all.
Reflection sees only a shallow layer and is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size, so scatter correction (MSC/SNV) and a flush mount in flowing product are needed.

methods.why: Preferred for transparent or semi-transparent liquids such as whey, and the volume sampled gives a representative signature for dilute streams.
Used inline for opaque or concentrated dairy products, with scatter correction before PLS for fat and protein.
Low-cost and highly sensitive for intrinsic fluorophores of biological origin, and can be combined with NIR to add specificity.
They add molecular specificity NIR may miss, but Raman can be masked by fluorescence and MIR ATR samples only a few micrometres.

experiment.objective: Compare NIR transmission/transflection and NIR diffuse reflection on whey and concentrate samples and decide one interface and one calibration per stream.
steps: Collect whey and concentrate samples that cover the expected composition range, and analyse each one independently in the laboratory for protein and fat.
Measure each sample with a transflection probe at a controlled path length and with a diffuse-reflection probe, on the same NIR spectrometer.
Optionally record fluorescence on the same samples to screen whether it adds information.
Apply MSC/SNV scatter correction, build a PLS model per stream and per interface, and validate on independent samples.
Compare validated performance per stream against the client's criteria and choose the interface and installation point.
references: Independent laboratory protein analysis of each sample
Independent laboratory fat analysis of each sample

lab_test: Raman or MIR ATR (only if needed)
pathway.key_features: No spectra have been supplied yet; the band chart places fat/protein/moisture at 0.85-1.1 µm, a candidate region to confirm in the lab test.
pathway.path_reason: The AFS pathway starts with multi-method lab trials and key-feature selection before choosing a model, a system or sensors.

multispectral.why: Milk is a complex medium that may need two methods, and fluorescence can add molecular specificity to NIR's broad bands for major components; in a cited fermentation example, NIR+fluorescence gave more accurate biomass.
multispectral.probe: Separate time-synchronised probes for the flowing liquid, unless the concentrate turns out to be heterogeneous at the probe scale, in which case a combined same-spot probe is needed
multispectral.fusion: Model per method first, then low-level fusion of synchronised spectra using dedicated data-fusion algorithms
multispectral.test: The fused model must beat the best single NIR model per stream on the same independent validation samples.

assumptions: Protein and fat are the main composition variables for both streams.
Both streams flow in pipes or vats where a flush-mounted or inserted probe can be installed.
